chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Arrangements and arrangers: Danny Mendelson and Buster Harding
summary: Wilson names his charts such as 'Sweet Lorraine', originals by Webster and Rudy Powell, and arranger Danny Mendelson.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Name a couple of the arrangements, Teddy, that you did. 'Sweet Lorraine' was one of them.
Yeah, that was one of my arrangements, 'Sweet Lorraine.'
Oh, I can sing those sax@phone parts, man.
And Ben Webster did an original for us, called '77', and that was just a number in the book and Rudy Powell did an excellent original for us called "Coconut Groove."
But I did a great many current pop tunes that came out, as they were brand new. (PAUSE IN TAPE)

I had an excellent arranger named Danny Mendelson, a young white fellow from Newark, and he did quite a few of the current pop tunes that came out in those days, and he studied quite a bit of orchestration and some of the sounds of the band was largely responsible to Danny Mendelson.
Oh, beautiful; I didn't know him.
He died a young fellow, unfortunately; so did Buster.
After my big band broke up, Buster did a great amount of writing for Basie.
He came to Cab Calloway, too, he did a lot of stuff for us.
Uh huh, yes. Buster was a very talented man.
And he was a swinging piano player, too.
He was out of Cleveland, wasn't he?
